position_summary: Strongest rival here. Retained review is anchored in non-delegable obligations codified across audit, bank credit/model risk, legal practice, engineering, nuclear and environmental regimes. In several regimes independence explicitly requires re-derivation that traceability cannot substitute for (UK highway checking without exchange of calculations; NRC alternate calculations). Where standards scale review intensity, they scale it by risk, significance and producer competence/objectivity, not by how traceable the producer's evidence is. On this reading the irreducible W1 core is large and transparency changes the inputs to review more than its amount.
holds_under_conditions: Regulated or legally exposed recipients (banks, auditors, lawyers, licensees) and high-consequence decisions; recipients who must demonstrate their own effective challenge to supervisors or courts. Weaker for unregulated equity investors whose IC review is policy- rather than law-driven.
would_change_my_view_if: Time-and-motion or file-review data showed that, with obligations held constant, recipients' review hours on advisor work fall substantially when the advisor file is traceable (e.g., auditors or credit officers documenting effective challenge largely by inspecting linked evidence), or supervisors/inspectors explicitly accepted traceable advisor files as sufficient evidence of the recipient's own challenge.
strength_of_evidence_note: Strong for the existence and breadth of obligations (about 17 independent groups, mostly primary standards and court decisions), but these are stated obligations, not observed time allocation. No source decomposes recipient hours into W1 versus W2. Several standards also permit reliance on documented work (EVR003, EVR067, EVR051), which is the thesis-friendly reading of the same corpus.

position_summary: Limitation rather than refutation. The mechanism (opacity and missing inputs create extra recipient work) is well attested, but no source measures the reducible W2 share in an advisor-to-investment-recipient workflow. The one quantified item (repeat imaging when outside images are not imported) concerns data availability and system integration, not reasoning transparency. Some of what looks like 'reconstruction' is the recipient forming the independent understanding that W1 regimes require (effective challenge, independent checking), so labelling it avoidable presupposes the obligation permits reliance.
holds_under_conditions: Holds wherever obligations require the recipient's own understanding or independent derivation; weaker where recipients may rely on documented producer work subject to risk-scaled evaluation.
would_change_my_view_if: Activity sampling or think-aloud logs of credit/IC analysts reviewing the same independent-engineer or advisor report with and without linked inputs showed a large share of time spent locating or re-deriving inputs, falling with traceability while seeded-error detection held steady.
strength_of_evidence_note: Mechanism evidence is moderate (about 9 groups, cross-domain, largely stated or qualitative). Magnitude evidence in the target workflow is absent; WS2 states W2 is acknowledged but not measured. Absence of measurement is not evidence that the share is small.

position_summary: Rival: W3 is a rational driver of review, and the evidence shows advisor-type outputs are materially wrong often enough to justify independent re-performance of high-risk items. Detection in the strongest cases came from outcome data or independent re-reads of primary data, not from inspecting the producer's citations. If W3 is material, the efficient response is targeted re-derivation, which traceability supports but does not remove.
holds_under_conditions: Domains with documented forecast bias or discrepancy rates (solar P50 estimates, outside pathology/imaging reads, AI-assisted drafting with fabricated references).
would_change_my_view_if: Data showed lender haircuts or re-review intensity do not vary with advisor track record or error rates (pointing to ritual or policy rather than W3), or showed that traceable files let recipients catch seeded material errors at re-performance rates for a fraction of the time.
strength_of_evidence_note: Moderate: about 9 independent groups, but the renewable-specific items are secondary (EVR047 news report; EVR048 search-summary lead only) and P50 provenance is unknown. The pathology studies show that most re-reviews change nothing (1.2-1.4% management changes), which cuts toward the thesis: coverage-based triage could target review.

position_summary: Rival: retained work is substantially criteria-driven. Rating agencies and banks apply their own cases and haircuts to advisor outputs, multi-user assurance reports may not fit a given user's assertions, preparers did not scope reports to recipients' materiality, and supervisors expect documented overlays and customization of vendor models. This W4 work persists however transparent the advisor is and limits what a generic product removes.
holds_under_conditions: Recipients with codified criteria (rating methodologies, credit policies, model-risk overlays) and reports prepared for multiple or unconsulted recipients.
would_change_my_view_if: Observed analyst workflows showed that most W4 effort is rebuilding advisor inputs (exceedance tables, loss breakdowns) before applying in-house haircuts, and that supplying adjustable structured inputs collapses that effort. WS2 identified this W2/W4 boundary as untested.
strength_of_evidence_note: Moderate for existence (about 5-6 groups), weak for magnitude: methodologies and guidance describe what recipients do, not how long it takes. Fitch criteria items are dated or presentation-based.

position_summary: Partially conceded with a limitation: W5 appears real, but the evidence is thin and points to customer specificity (memo templates 'practically never the same'), which bears on repeatability more than on the thesis. Board-pack evidence is vendor-sourced and about recipients' own reporting, not advisor outputs.
holds_under_conditions: Investment organizations with bespoke IC templates; board reporting contexts.
would_change_my_view_if: Activity sampling showed a large, stable share of analyst hours spent fitting third-party reports into IC templates, with template structures converging across firms.
strength_of_evidence_note: Weak: one 54-organization survey with interview-based time estimates, one job posting, and vendor-linked board surveys accessed partly. Stated, not observed.

position_summary: Rival in a refined form: review serves functions beyond error detection (education, norms, comfort, accountability, defensive documentation), and professionals discount machine-sourced or other-sourced evidence for reasons beyond its content. But the regulator-observed failure mode is under-challenge, not over-review. The best-supported rival is therefore misdirected review: effort goes to step-by-step checking of provided detail while assumptions go unchallenged. Traceability that makes detail-checking easier could reinforce that pattern (analyst inference, untested).
holds_under_conditions: Accountability to audiences with known views, post-decision justification pressure, and recipients who verify the producer's numbers rather than challenge the producer's frame.
would_change_my_view_if: Field data showed recipients' review time and challenge of assumptions both responded to evidence quality (more challenge where evidence is weak, less where strong), with no residual source-based discounting once evidence specificity is equalized.
strength_of_evidence_note: Moderate: about 10 groups, but several are secondary or abstract-level (EVR157 via secondary summary; EVR025, EVR029 abstract-level), and code-review studies are a weak analog. EVR033 cuts both ways: more specific memos erased source-based discounting, but without ground truth, so this is reliance, not accuracy.

position_summary: Rival: verification-time reductions from provenance aids are real but small-sample, lab-based, and at least partly explained by reduced scrutiny. In the highlight study, time fell about 25% while accuracy fell when the model was wrong. Reading retrieved passages took about 2.5 times longer than reading explanations, with equal accuracy. Attribution judging stays slow for long sources. In naturalistic use, links are rarely followed. Time savings may come from checking less, not from checking more cheaply.
holds_under_conditions: Lay or student participants, short tasks, and producers that are sometimes wrong; untested with professional reviewers of advisor reports.
would_change_my_view_if: A randomized study with credit/IC professionals and seeded material errors showed traceable reports cut time per finding while detection rate and correct-rejection rate held or improved, including on trials where the advisor was wrong.
strength_of_evidence_note: Weak-to-moderate either way: about 9 relevant groups, none with professionals reviewing a real advisor deliverable (WS7 flags this as absence of evidence). EVR109 (accuracy preserved, provenance correct by construction, no inferential statistics) is the best pro-thesis item.

position_summary: Rival: detection is preserved only conditionally. Aids help when verification is cheaper than solving and when the producer is right; when the producer is wrong, explanation and highlight designs lowered detection in several independent studies. Explanations of a biased AI did not mitigate the bias. The one higher-evidence structured-reporting cohort found less accurate, less complete reports. Average-accuracy nulls conceal a right-versus-wrong asymmetry, which is the case that matters for error detection.
holds_under_conditions: Producer accuracy below ceiling, aids that make acceptance easier than checking, and errors that are not visible in the cited evidence (omissions, misgrounded citations).
would_change_my_view_if: Seeded-error studies with professionals showed traceable/coverage-explicit reports preserve detection on producer-wrong trials (no asymmetry) and reduce missed omissions.
strength_of_evidence_note: Mixed. About 9-10 groups on each side; most are lay or student human-AI tasks, which WS7 and EVR176/EVR180 flag as weakly transferable. No test with seeded errors in advisor deliverables.

position_summary: Rival strongly supported: citations and explanations raise trust and acceptance more reliably than they improve detection. Even random citations raised trust and fewer than 10% of cited answers were checked; perceived utility was inversely related to citation precision across systems; links were rarely clicked yet users reported relying on them; graders rated AI-assisted incorrect answers higher; explanations increased acceptance of wrong advice; users preferred designs that protected them least. Satisfaction and trust therefore cannot serve as evidence of verification value.
holds_under_conditions: Self-reported trust outcomes; lay participants; consumer interfaces. Professional, accountable reviewers may check more, but this is untested.
would_change_my_view_if: Professional reviewers with accountability checked cited evidence at high rates, and checking rates and detection rose with citation availability rather than trust alone.
strength_of_evidence_note: Moderate-to-strong for the mechanism (about 10 independent groups, several preregistered or tracked-behavior), weak for transfer to accountable professionals (EVR176, EVR180).

position_summary: Limitation: coverage-visibility evidence is mostly mandates (obligation, not outcome) and producer-report completeness, not recipient appropriate reliance. Outcome evidence is mixed. Pre-filled 'normal' statements, the closest analog to boilerplate checks-without-findings, did not reduce errors and generated contradictions. The single highest-level structured-reporting study found no improvement. Reported coverage metrics in TAR diverged sharply from metrics recomputed from the underlying samples. Standard-setters decided no-deviation sample detail need not be disclosed. Coverage claims help only when verifiable and right-sized.
holds_under_conditions: Coverage statements that are templated, asserted without underlying data, or generated by the same system whose work they describe.
would_change_my_view_if: Omission-probe experiments with professionals showed coverage disclosures (incl. checks with no findings) increase detection of omitted checks and reduce redundant re-checking, without increasing acceptance of false 'no issue' statements.
strength_of_evidence_note: The pro-thesis side is broader here than on P2.1 to P2.3: court-accepted TAR validation substituting for item review (EVR069 to EVR071) is the strongest analog for coverage evidence replacing re-review, and synoptic completeness gains are consistent (EVR197, 13/14 studies). But those gains are in completeness of the producer's report, and TAR acceptance relied on statistical sampling plus adversarial access.

position_summary: Agreed limitation: citation-providing systems and professional advisors still produced unsupported, misgrounded or fabricated citations at material rates. Combined with low checking rates (P2.3), traceability can create false assurance unless the recipient actually checks, which reintroduces the work.
holds_under_conditions: Generative or retrieval-augmented drafting; misgrounded citations (real source, unsupported claim), which are harder to detect than fabrications.
would_change_my_view_if: Not a dispute with the thesis; would matter less if automated citation-support checks reached near-complete precision and recall on professional documents.
strength_of_evidence_note: Strong (about 8 groups including peer-reviewed audits, court decisions and government-contract incidents). Thesis-compatible: RAG tools hallucinated less than ungrounded models.

position_summary: Agreed: model rationales can be unfaithful. Extension (inference, untested): system-generated statements of what was checked could also be unfaithful, so coverage logs need independent verifiability rather than self-report.
would_change_my_view_if: Evidence that coverage logs derived from execution traces (not model narration) were faithful under audit.
strength_of_evidence_note: Moderate for chain-of-thought unfaithfulness (3 groups, one a working paper); no evidence on coverage-log faithfulness, which is absence of evidence.

position_summary: Rival: no direct end-to-end evidence in IC workflows exists in the register. Generic AI end-to-end evidence shows small savings that are reallocated, no measured productivity gain, and in one RCT longer completion times. Vendor 'days to hours' claims are unmeasured.
holds_under_conditions: Generic AI assistants and government or software settings; extrapolation to advisor-to-IC integration is analogy.
would_change_my_view_if: Matched-deal time logs from advisor report receipt to IC approval showed fewer analyst hours, fewer IC follow-up questions and equal or more errors caught with integration.
strength_of_evidence_note: Weak on both sides. EVR213 (imported images: 11% vs 52% repeat imaging, adjusted OR 9.0) is the best pro-thesis analog but observational and possibly confounded by workflow factors.

position_summary: Rival strongly supported: AI assistance and integration relocate work to verification, interrogation, coaching and cleanup; generate new tasks; and push costs onto recipients of polished but low-quality output. Even a strengthened specialist rule left specialist hours unchanged, shifting them to planning.
holds_under_conditions: Imperfect producers; tasks where verification is costly; organizations without redesigned review processes.
would_change_my_view_if: End-to-end measurement showed verification added by integration is smaller than drafting and reformatting removed, net of rework downstream.
strength_of_evidence_note: Moderate: about 13 independent groups (workslop items are one group), but mostly generic AI tools and self-report; relevance to advisor deliverables is by mechanism.

position_summary: Limitation: separability of drafting from judgment rests mainly on stated preference and vendor or practitioner claims. Observed tasks show summarising gains but worse accuracy on slide and spreadsheet work, an RCT showed only slight speed gains with inconsistent quality, and the memo itself is where judgment is expressed (authors flag consultant-written memos as a governance concern). The reducible part may be the lowest-value part.
holds_under_conditions: Formatting/drafting tasks that embed analytic choices (what to include, how to frame risk).
would_change_my_view_if: Blind-graded IC memos showed AI- or advisor-populated sections preserved reviewer-identified judgment quality while cutting drafting hours.
strength_of_evidence_note: Weak: vendor case study and practitioner estimates (unmeasured), small-sample government observation, abstract-level RCT access.

position_summary: Rival: uptake rises with the ability to modify outputs even when modification is trivial, suggesting a sense-of-control mechanism rather than better evidence use. Supports adaptability as an adoption lever but not as evidence of appropriate reliance.
would_change_my_view_if: Professional settings showed modification rights increase use and accuracy, not just use.
strength_of_evidence_note: Weak: one underlying group (two records), lay participants.

position_summary: Supported, and it constrains the thesis commercially: heterogeneous criteria, templates, data formats and governance require per-customer configuration; templates that work were built with local teams, and national templates covered a minority of locally used concepts.
holds_under_conditions: Multi-recipient products; recipients with codified criteria.
would_change_my_view_if: Cross-customer data showed most configuration is shared, with a small customer-specific residue.
strength_of_evidence_note: Moderate for heterogeneity, mostly by radiology analogy plus one investment survey and one procurement list.

position_summary: Qualified: standardization is achievable within one organization with sustained effort, but standard formats leave low inter-observer agreement, partial template coverage, uneven adoption and a preference for adaptable rather than rigid structures. Multi-user assurance reports require users to assess fit and add procedures.
would_change_my_view_if: Evidence that one standardized evidence format served many recipients with low per-recipient adaptation and stable quality.
strength_of_evidence_note: Moderate, by analogy (radiology and pathology reporting, assurance standards); no direct supplier-delivery data.

position_summary: Rival: no register evidence links reduced recipient effort to buying, renewal or pricing. Satisfaction coexisted with no productivity evidence; purchase cases were framed as break-even thresholds with savings unmeasured; procurement weighted technical capability over cost with per-project pricing. One field experiment showed follow-on consulting purchases, but for operational consulting, not verification effort.
would_change_my_view_if: Buyer renewal or pricing data tied to measured recipient-effort reductions.
strength_of_evidence_note: Very weak either way; this is absence of evidence, not evidence of absence.
